summary: A Fabric grant refusal on a fallback route no longer pins the replication worker to it: the worker holds the refused route for 30 minutes and goes back to the preferred route at once, on that route's own back-off, so one failed tailnet exchange during a member's restart no longer stalls replication for hours (#4152)

schema.detail: No table, index, migration or wire change; the hold is worker memory.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Only the local worker's route choice changes. A refused preferred route still stays selected with normal peer back-off and is never bypassed through a fallback. The status shows `refused` until another route exchanges, then `up`, with the refused attempt kept as the last failed exchange. Members on older builds exchange as before.

manual.detail: Nothing to configure. A member stalled by this today recovers when its replication worker restarts on the new build.

recovery.detail: The hold lives only in worker memory; an older build returns to the previous route choice.
